lead.hed: Defense News: Ukraine asks the EU to fund its first PAC-3 Patriot buy
lead.insight: Defense News, Saturday: Kyiv asked to tap a €90 billion EU support loan for PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot batteries — the first formal request to use that loan for the U.S.-made missiles. Because PAC-3s are built in the United States, the purchase needs an exemption from the loan’s non-EU content cap. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the review was moving and that EU representatives were due to decide Monday.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Army photo by Maj. Nicholas Chopp · DVIDS 7275187 · Public domain · A PAC-2 Patriot interceptor launches during a live-fire exercise in Palau, June 15, 2022.

political.hed: USNI: U.S. and Iran trade strikes along the Strait of Hormuz
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: the United States resumed attacking Iranian targets along the Strait of Hormuz this week. Central Command posted video on X saying it hit Iranian targets, including two unidentified ships. The item is a CENTCOM release plus Iranian counter-messaging.

political.hed: Defense News: Air Force speeds a cheaper Reaper successor after Iran losses
political.insight: Defense News, Friday: Lt. Gen. Christopher Niemi said Sept. 3 the Air Force is accelerating a cheaper, more expendable follow-on to the MQ-9A Reaper after combat losses. Officials did not announce a new fielding date. The Massed Modular Aircraft competition is the named path; a fully missionized aircraft is still unpriced.

political.hed: Defense News: RAND says the U.S. lacks hands to rebuild wartime satellites
political.insight: Defense News, Friday: RAND’s Aug. 31 report “Breaking Glass, Missing Hands” says the United States does not have enough engineers, technicians, and assemblers to rebuild military satellites in 12 to 24 months after a war with China or Russia. Gen. Michael Guetlein sponsored the study as vice chief of space operations.

tech.hed: AP: xAI sues Minnesota over the state’s AI nudification ban
tech.insight: Associated Press: xAI sued Monday over Minnesota’s first-in-the-nation ban on AI “nudification” tools, which takes effect Saturday. The company says it does not contest a ban on non-consensual AI nudes, but argues the law is overbroad, has no good-faith safe harbor, and sets a $500,000 penalty per violation.

tech.hed: NVIDIA at IFA: local agents, PAIR routing, RTX Spark in October
tech.insight: NVIDIA, Thursday vendor post from IFA: local agents get simpler setup on RTX hardware, RTX Spark Windows PCs arrive in October, and NVIDIA PAIR can route inference across idle PCs. The post names Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and Perplexity Portable Computer.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: bad publicity can still find the quiet builders
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: “The Benefits of Bad Publicity” says a public fight can surface neighbors who are already doing the work — educators and parents building classical schools instead of performing online. The essay points to Texas’s Valor Schools, with five campuses and thousands on a waitlist.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: a new Reykjavik film puts Reagan back on screen
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: a review of The Brink of War, focused on the 1986 Reykjavik summit. The piece says Jeff Daniels’s Reagan is unusually sympathetic, and that the film treats the Strategic Defense Initiative as the point Reagan would not trade away.
